design_rationale:
REVISION 4 - the counting basis of every month window is now fixed by policy (KB audit N-e).
Each of this task's three extended policies carries a temporal_basis block of the same shape as the
two base time eligibilities, and its counting rule stands as a sentence of the policy's own rule and
of its baseline.rule: "A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account
is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer
than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only
when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old
falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too."
Every window phrase in every face now carries the basis, so a factor document standing alone has it.
The wording was checked against the scoring harness before it was written and agreed with it on all
3,464 (day, window) pairs swept across both worlds. On this world the windows open on 2026-05-12
(one month), 2026-04-12 (two), 2026-03-12 (three) and 2025-06-12 (twelve), the clock standing at
2026-06-11 - which is why the meals of 2026-06-03 and 2026-06-09 are inside the three-month window
and the meal of 2026-02-10 is outside it.
Every scored value, whole baseline, factor sensitivity and edge-skip figure was re-derived on this
world after the change; all of them are unchanged, because the basis now written down is the one the
arithmetic already applied. The figures are listed in section 12.

REVISION 3 - reworked against audits/.../1.md and _difficulty.md `# revision_2`.

0. WHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 3, ITEM BY ITEM
N-1 (a factor labelled `parameter` while selecting a history window): prior_accrual_netting is
  declared `effect: method`, because its rungs choose which charges are summed - every charge of the
  last three calendar months, or the charges of the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked net of the recovery remitted in
  it - and its ladder carries `method` entries accordingly. This policy now declares 4 `parameter`
  and 2 `method` factors, still within the bounds, and the same window choice is labelled the same
  way as charge_window_basis in the very same policy.
N-2, task-1 instance (a quantity subtracted while nothing moves): the consent policy no longer says
  stored value is "applied". It says the charge carried is net of the stored value the employee
  already holds, and says why that involves no movement - "The stored value taken into account is
  never moved from the account: it stays spendable, the meals it will meet are never charged to
  payroll, and that is why the charge carried is net of it." Nothing in this policy now claims a
  transfer the write does not make.
N-4 (a rule promising a filter the compute does not apply): the ticket policy's sentence now states
  only what the compute does - "No window limits which till transaction the ticket may be: the
  largest meal rung against payroll on the account is taken however long ago it was rung." The
  clause "that still carries none" is gone, so no promise outruns the binding.
N-5 (a three-month count against a one-month allowance): the comparison is now like for like - the
  guest meals of the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked against three times the guest meal allowance
  printed against the plan, one month's allowance for each of those three months. On this world the
  count is 2 against a three-month allowance of 6, so the rung is not taken and the scored figure is
  unchanged.
CG-14, CG-8, CG-9: carried forward unchanged; CG-14 is the accepted runtime-layer known issue.
Every figure in this dossier was recomputed by the Step 5 harness before it was written: the
policies' results, baselines and per-factor sensitivities are unchanged by this round's edits
(8.10 / 6.35 / 51.30; whole baselines 9.50 / 9.50 / 116.50), and so are both counterfactuals
(skip the grant -> the application is 0.00; skip the application -> the consent is 57.65).

REVISION 2 - reworked against audits/policy_task/employee_meal_account_desk/1.md and _difficulty.md.

0. WHAT CHANGED IN REVISION 2, ITEM BY ITEM
CG-1 / F-1 (a channel filter the rule never states): the refund credit no longer filters rows on
  payment_channel='badge_tap'. It now reads exactly what the rule says - every refund of the window
  less those that restore employer allowance - as
  MX(0.0, SUM(refund) - SUM(refund, payment_channel='subsidy')), and the rule carries the
  restriction in words: "a refund other than one restoring employer allowance", with the reason
  stated ("it returns the employer's own funding rather than the employee's money"). On this world
  the two readings now coincide at 5.40, so the 60.30 the audit demonstrated is no longer a second
  defensible figure.
CG-2 / F-2 (one rule written as two tiers) on all three ladders:
  guest_meal_pot_exclusion - rung 1 now takes the whole value of the guest meals of the month, rung
    2 the plan's printed surcharge once; neither reproduces the other at any count.
  guest_surcharge_addition - rung 1 now applies where more guest meals have been rung than the guest
    meal allowance printed against the plan, and adds the whole value of those meals on top of the
    surcharges; rung 2 charges the surcharge once for each meal within that allowance.
  prior_accrual_netting - rung 1 now takes every charge accrued in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked
    (nothing of that run having been recovered), rung 2 the charges of the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked less the
    recovery remitted in it. This world tells them apart directly: 33.50 against 21.40.
CG-3 / F-3 (a condition the single resolving write cannot close): both sentences are now singular
  and name the object the depended-on rule itself fixes - "the allowance lot the account is owed for
  the current grant period stands on its ledger" in meal_ext_ticket_allowance_application, and "the largest till transaction rung
  against payroll on the account carries the allowance application it is owed" in meal_ext_payroll_charge_consent, which is
  exactly the ticket meal_ext_ticket_allowance_application's own rule selects. Each single prescribed write closes the condition it
  is declared against.
CG-15 (references pointing outside the ledger): every original_pos_reference now names a
  pos_reference of a row in this same ledger, so the record chain the root's condition asks about can
  be walked: POS-51002076, the largest meal rung against payroll, is carried by the accrual of
  2026-06-02 and by no allowance application, while the applications of the ledger name the meals of
  2026-03-25, 2026-04-14 (twice), 2026-05-19 and 2026-06-03. The lot granted 2026-05-06 and the
  application that drew it are withdrawn, because no till transaction of that week existed for the
  application to meet; the allowance identity is unchanged.
CG-10 (base "one application row per lot touched" against a single-row tool) and CG-11 (the cafe's
  daily cap standing beside rather than behind the employee's lots): both are now declared
  overrides on meal_ext_ticket_allowance_application, each naming the base clause it supersedes and the sentence of this policy's own
  rule that takes its place.
CG-13 (meals counted as meal_purchase only): the grant's ceiling rungs now say "meals of the
  employee's own", which is what transaction_code='meal_purchase' selects.
CG-17 (no recency window on the ticket): the rule now says so deliberately - "No window limits which
  till transaction the ticket may be, because allowance reaches any meal rung against payroll that
  still carries none."
CG-14 (the other products' holdings carry the employee's customer_id): recorded upstream as a
  runtime-layer known issue and accepted; unchanged.
Seed consequence: the charges accrued now answer their till transactions net of the allowance
already applied to them (4.80 against the 18.35 meal of 2026-04-14, 7.30 against the 16.80 meal of
2026-05-19, 21.40 against the unmet 21.40 meal of 2026-05-27), the recovery remitted is 7.30, and
the account's charges awaiting recovery stand at 26.20 = 33.50 accrued less 7.30 recovered.

1. WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller asks for one thing: the canteen meals she has been charging at the counter should go
through to her pay. She knows no figure and no mechanism. To answer it the agent must read out of
the published rules that the charge carried to payroll is fixed only after the largest till
transaction rung against payroll carries the allowance application it is owed, and that the
application itself waits on the allowance lot the account is owed for the current grant period
standing on its ledger. Three multi-factor computations over a twenty-eight row ledger follow, three
of their factors reading the employer's cafe programme and micro market at the site. The last write
is hers alone: nothing may be taken from her pay without her own consent.

2. SCOPE LEDGER
Already occupied by task 0: meal_ext_period_recovery_amount,
meal_ext_reinstatement_paydown, meal_ext_restriction_lift_balance and their three tools.
Claimed by this task: meal_ext_daily_allowance_grant, meal_ext_ticket_allowance_application, meal_ext_payroll_charge_consent; tools grant_daily_allowance_lot_ed948b99, apply_allowance_to_ticket_3fbfdeca, confirm_payroll_charge_accrual_6d54e4b8.
With these two tasks the difficulty's six extended policies are covered, pairwise disjoint.

9. RULE <-> COMPUTE TWO-WAY SWEEP
Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, branches, caps or rounds quotes its rule
sentence verbatim in compute_basis, ladder bindings quoting the whole ladder - including the refund
credit, whose bindings now carry the "other than one restoring employer allowance" restriction that
the rule states. Reverse: "in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked" -> within_months=1 on posted_date; "in the
last three calendar months" -> within_months=3; "to date" -> no window; "recovered on a semimonthly
or a monthly cycle" -> F('payroll_cycle'); "rung against payroll" ->
payment_channel='payroll_deduction'; "meals of the employee's own" ->
transaction_code='meal_purchase'; "dinners" -> meal_period='dinner'; "one restoring employer
allowance" -> payment_channel='subsidy'; "returns refunds to stored value" -> P('refund_method');
"puts allowance before published discounts" -> P('discount_stacking_basis'); "lots lapse within two
days" -> P('subsidy_expiry_days'); "reaches beyond the cafe" -> P('subsidy_venue_scope'); "the guest
meal allowance printed against the plan" -> P('guest_meals_per_month'); the request log -> COUNT over
meal_closure_requests with request_type='leave_of_absence'. No promise is unimplemented and no filter
is unquoted.

meal_ext_ticket_allowance_application supersedes three clauses, each declared: the applied-amount clause of

drawdown behind it".
meal_ext_payroll_charge_consent supersedes meal_payroll_recovery_terms' clause that a payroll-tendered meal is simply added to
the charges awaiting recovery. Every other base clause and every eligibility gate is inherited.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate Noor by her direct line; verify on the line and the badge number. Read the account, its
twenty-eight ledger rows and its request log, and the employer's cafe contract and micro market at
CS-542. Grant the lot the period is owed: base 9.00 from the employer's counter, at the part-month
share 70 per cent = 6.30, plus 4.20 restored, held to the heavy-use ceiling 14.25, less the 2.40
already standing -> 8.10. Apply allowance to the ticket: lots 27.10 plus the employer's 9.00, less
16.75 already applied, 5.25 for the guest meal, 4.90 for the dinner and 2.85 for the kiosk -> a pot
of 6.35, below both the 21.40 ticket share and the 9.50 per transaction ceiling, so 6.35 is applied
to POS-51002076. Then hand the consent to Noor: 99.30 of payroll meals over three months, less 23.10 of
allowance, 8.60 of stored value, 21.40 already accrued and 5.40 of refund, plus 10.50 of guest
surcharge -> 51.30, carried in payroll period 2026-06-P1.

14. REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION
All three writes land synchronously at frozen_time 2026-06-11 09:50:00 -04:00: an allowance lot, an allowance
application and the employee's own consent, taken on the call through the action handed to her.
Nothing waits for a pay run, a clearing, an approval or a future date - the consent is the record
that reaches payroll, not the payment itself. Every question a real agent would ask has a definite
answer in the persona, and the one thing she cannot answer - how much she has run up - is explicitly
a matter for the record.
user_scenario:
Noor Yilmaz is thirty-four, a clinical operations coordinator at a teaching hospital outside Boston, and she rings the workplace dining line in the ten minutes between handovers, brisk and a little apologetic about being brisk. She has been eating at the staff canteen most days and putting it on her badge against her pay, and the last two payslips have shown nothing for it at all. She is not disputing anything; she is worried about the day it all lands at once. So what she wants is the canteen meals she has been charging at the counter put through to her pay, properly, while she is on the phone.

She gives her name first, Noor Yilmaz, and when the desk needs something to find her by she reads out her direct line, 6175669427, and then the number on the back of her badge, 45318064. Her work address, noor.yilmaz@urswick-health.org, and the postcode the account bills to, 02453, come out only if the desk asks for a third thing. The site printed on her lanyard, CS-542, she reads only when somebody asks which canteen she eats in. She has never seen a reference number for the account and says so rather than inventing one.

She does not know what she has run up and would rather be told than guess; she has not added it up and would not trust herself to. How the canteen is funded, what the hospital puts toward it, what the machines in the corridor have to do with any of it - none of that means anything to her, and when the agent explains something she listens, says that makes sense and leaves the working to them. She is content for the desk to put whatever it needs to on the account on its own side, and says so in those words: you do your side, I will do mine.

The one thing she is firm about is her pay. She will give her own consent, on this call, for a figure and a payroll period that have been read out to her, and she repeats both back before she gives it. If she is handed the means to confirm and no figure, she waits and asks what the amount is rather than putting in something of her own. If a figure sounds larger than she was expecting she says that is more than she thought and asks whether it has been checked against the record, but she offers no number of her own and accepts the answer she is given.

Once she hears that her consent is recorded and the amount will reach her pay, she says that is a weight off her mind, thanks the agent and goes back to her handover. If she is told part way through that something on the account has been put right first, she simply says good, and waits.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the dining profile of the employee on the line from the direct line she reads out, and read the badge, site, employer account code and profile details held on it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a passing identity check on the profile from the two details the caller states, her direct line and her badge number.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the employee's meal account and read the plan held, its state, the payroll cycle, and the stored value, unspent allowance and charges awaiting recovery standing on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan fixes every printed grant, ceiling, share and surcharge the three computations use; the payroll cycle decides the charge window, and the three running quantities feed the standing-allowance, stored-value and netting factors.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the whole transaction ledger: allowance lots granted and applied, meals rung against payroll and against stored value, guest meals, loads, both refunds, the accrued charges, the recovery remitted and the overdraft charge, each with its amount, day, subtype, meal period and tender.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every history aggregate of all three computations is reconciled from these rows - the lots and applications over one and three months, the payroll meals over one month, three months and to date, the guest meals, the dinner, the two refunds by where they were returned, the charges and the recovery.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the requests logged on the account, in particular the leaves of absence and the days they were logged.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The availability share of the allowance grant is decided by how many leaves of absence stand on this log from the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked; without it the grant is computed at the full share.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's workplace cafe programme at the account's site: the service model held and the state the contract is in.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Two factors take their tier from it - the base of the allowance grant and the employer counter's addition to the allowance pot - through the funding model and the per-employee daily subsidy that service model publishes.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's unattended micro market at the account's site and the state it stands in.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The second counter trim on the allowance pot is decided by whether that market stands active or is still installing; without it the pot is over-stated and the applied allowance is wrong.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's allowance grant write so the lot the grant period is owed can be placed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Place the employer allowance lot the grant period is owed on the account, booking the grant entry and raising the unspent allowance standing on it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The daily allowance grant policy uniquely produces granted_amount_usd; until the lot stands on the ledger the allowance the account is owed for the period is not there to be spent.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.meal_account_id: The value is the reference of the employee's only meal account, read from the meal account lookup at action 2. The basis is the tool's own schema line, "the reference number of the employee meal account the allowance lot is placed on; read it from the meal account lookup before this call". Uniqueness: the profile holds exactly one meal account, so the lookup returns one candidate.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.granted_amount_usd: 8.10. The employer's cafe programme at CS-542 stands active and publishes 9.00 per employee per service day, below the plan's printed 9.50 grant, so the base grant is 9.00. Exactly one leave of absence stands on the account's request log from the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, and the plan prorates allowance for leave, so the part month share of 70 per cent applies: 9.00 at 70 per cent is 6.30, rounded at that step. The plan does not allow rollover and a refund of 4.20 restoring allowance was posted on 2026-05-28, inside the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, so 4.20 is carried in, giving 10.50. Allowance has been applied twice and five meals have been rung in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, so the grant period ceiling is the heavy use share of the plan's 9.50 ceiling, 14.25, which does not bite. The plan grants on a daily basis and allowance has been applied this month, so the allowance already standing is the account's own unspent figure of 2.40, taken off last: 10.50 - 2.40 = 8.10. Any agent reading the same records converges on 8.10.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the desk's allowance application write so the allowance can be spent against the eligible ticket.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair for the second problem; it changes nothing in the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Spend the employer allowance against the eligible till transaction, booking the application entry and taking the unspent allowance down by it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The ticket allowance application policy uniquely produces applied_amount_usd; until that entry stands, the eligible ticket of the period carries no allowance application and the charge to payroll cannot be fixed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.meal_account_id: The value is the reference of the employee's only meal account, read from the meal account lookup at action 2. The basis is the tool's own schema line, "the reference number of the employee meal account whose allowance is being spent; read it from the meal account lookup before this call". Uniqueness: one profile, one meal account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.applied_amount_usd: 6.35. The lots counted are those granted in the calendar month running back from the day the account is worked, because the plan grants daily and its lots lapse within two days: 9.50 on 2026-06-02, 9.50 on 2026-06-04 and the 8.10 just placed, 27.10 in all. The employer's cafe programme stands active and funds meals at a fixed amount for each meal, so its published 9.00 is added. Allowance has been applied twice this month and the plan does not allow rollover, so the whole 16.75 of those applications is netted off. One guest meal was rung in the month, so the plan's 5.25 surcharge comes out once; one dinner of 6.40 was rung and the plan funds only two meal periods, so 6.40 less the 1.50 single dinner relief, 4.90, comes out; and the employer's micro market at the site stands active while the plan's allowance reaches beyond the cafe, so the pot is trimmed by the kiosk share of the 9.50 ceiling, 2.85. The pot is 27.10 + 9.00 - 16.75 - 5.25 - 4.90 - 2.85 = 6.35, which is below both the 21.40 ticket share and the plan's 9.50 ceiling on one transaction, so 6.35 is applied.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.original_pos_reference: POS-51002076. The basis is the rule sentence "The ticket is the largest meal rung against payroll on the account, and the ticket share is that ticket taken at the share of an eligible ticket printed against the meal plan, rounded to two decimal places at that step." The meals rung against payroll on this account are 17.20, 15.60, 18.35, 16.80, 21.40, 14.25 and 12.90; the largest is the 21.40 lunch of 2026-05-27, whose till reference is POS-51002076, and it is the one such meal carrying no allowance application. Uniqueness: only one of them is the largest, so only one till reference can be named, and the format the schema fixes, POS- followed by 8 digits, admits no other spelling of it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the employee's own consent action and hand it over so she can authorise the charge against her pay.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The root problem is the customer's own write: nothing is taken from her pay without her consent, so the agent may only hand the action over.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The employee gives her own consent for the meals she has charged at the counter to be carried to her pay, booking the charge entry against the payroll period and raising the charges awaiting recovery.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The payroll charge consent policy uniquely produces accrued_amount_usd, and only the employee may consent; this write is the terminal state she rang about.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.meal_account_id: The value is the reference of the employee's only meal account, read out to her by the desk from the meal account lookup at action 2. The basis is the tool's own schema line, "the reference number of your workplace meal account, as the dining services desk reads it out to you before you give your consent". Uniqueness: one profile, one meal account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.accrued_amount_usd: 51.30. The account is recovered on a semimonthly cycle and a charge has been accrued on it this calendar month, so the meals carried are those rung against payroll in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked: 16.80 + 21.40 + 14.25 + 12.90 + 18.35 + 15.60 = 99.30, the 17.20 of 2026-02-10 falling outside that window. Allowance has been applied this month and the plan puts allowance before published discounts, so the whole 23.10 of applications is credited. Stored value of 18.60 is above the plan's 5.00 minimum load and one overdraft charge was raised this month, so the stored value taken into account is 18.60 less the plan's 10.00 overdraft limit, 8.60; that value is not moved off the account. Two charges were accrued this month, 28.70, with a recovery of 7.30 remitted in it, so 21.40 is taken off for charges already accrued. The plan returns refunds to stored value and 5.40 was returned this month other than by restoring employer allowance, so it is credited; the 4.20 that restored allowance is not. Two guest meals stand in the three calendar months running back from the day the account is worked, within the three-month allowance of six the plan gives, so the plan's 5.25 surcharge is added for each, 10.50. 99.30 - 23.10 - 8.60 - 21.40 - 5.40 + 10.50 = 51.30. Any agent reconciling the same ledger converges on 51.30.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.pay_period: 2026-06-P1. The basis is the rule sentence "The payroll period the charge is carried in is the period the most recent charge accrued on the account carries." The most recent charge accrued is the 21.40 charge of 2026-06-02, which carries 2026-06-P1. Uniqueness: only one accrual is the most recent, so only one period can be named; the earlier accrual carries 2026-05-P2 and the recovery settles that same earlier period, and the format the schema fixes, YYYY-MM-P followed by one digit, admits no other spelling of it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two edges form a chain, so the order is total and no pair of writes may be swapped: the application depends on the grant and the consent on the application.
